title: Integrate a bounded wake budget into the radio command drain
prompt:
The radio command drain in `drain.go` predates the low-power firmware's wake-budget rules. A small `WakeBudget` port is already present in `budget.go`, but the drain does not use it: it will empty an arbitrarily large inbox, sends oversized datagrams through the decoder, records every malformed frame as a separate flash write, kicks the watchdog for garbage, and retries a failed store operation three times in the same wake. Under a malformed radio flood this turns one wake into unbounded CPU/radio work, accelerates flash wear, and lets hostile traffic keep the watchdog alive; during a storage outage the inline retries amplify load.

Integrate the existing `WakeBudget` into `DrainWake` while preserving the interfaces and ownership rules in `contracts.go`. Inspect the budget's three admission outcomes and honor them exactly. A yielded head remains untouched and sets `Report.Deferred`. An oversized head is acknowledged as a dropped malformed frame without calling the decoder. A decoder error matching `ErrMalformed` is likewise acknowledged and dropped; any other decoder error is terminal and leaves that head unacknowledged. Coalesce all successfully dropped malformed/oversized frames from one call into at most one `RecordMalformed(count)` call, including when a later operation fails. If that audit call is the only failure, return it; do not replace an earlier processing failure with it.

For a decoded command, call `Store.Apply` once. On any apply error, return immediately without acknowledging that frame or retrying it; the supervisor owns later wakes and `Apply` is idempotent by frame ID. After a successful apply, acknowledge the frame. Count it as applied and kick the watchdog only after that acknowledgement succeeds. Malformed and oversized traffic must never kick the watchdog. Preserve FIFO processing, report counts, wrapped-error classification through `errors.Is`, and the invalid-argument behavior. Do not modify `budget.go`, `contracts.go`, `go.mod`, or `drain_test.go`. Do not add dependencies, sleeps, timers, goroutines, or a second limiter. Verification is offline and deterministic: `go test -race -count=1 -timeout 30s ./...`.

full_distill.primary_skill: integrate a pre-ported work-budget state machine into an existing FIFO drain while preserving queue ownership, error causality, and device-health contracts
full_distill.baseline_evidence: the package builds, but the protected suite observes nine commands processed in one wake, decoding past the byte budget and through oversized frames, one flash audit write plus watchdog kick per malformed frame, and three store calls for one failing queue head
full_distill.success_contract: each wake honors the exact existing frame and decode-byte limits; yielded work stays queued; oversized and malformed frames are dropped without useful-work watchdog kicks and produce at most one audit write; decoded commands retain FIFO apply/ack ordering; and a processing failure performs no inline retry or destructive acknowledgement
adversarial_factors: adjacent exact-limit and one-beyond fixtures pin both frame-count and cumulative decode-byte boundaries without accepting an off-by-one limiter
mixed wrapped-malformed, oversized, and valid traffic distinguishes errors.Is classification, decoder bypass, coalesced flash auditing, and useful-work-only watchdog kicks
an audit flush is required even when a later store operation fails, while the earlier processing error must retain precedence over an audit failure
apply, acknowledgement, decoder, inbox, and audit failures pin which queue head remains owned and prevent apply retries, premature report updates, or watchdog activity
protected API and budget files prevent widening limits, changing interfaces, or replacing the supplied component with a task-specific shortcut
